evidence.quote: During our open hours, you can drop into the Math Center in Kraemer Family Library 211, or chat with a tutor live in MS Teams.

question: can i get math center tutoring online instead of going to campus?
reference_answer: Yes. Math Center tutoring is available in person and online through Microsoft Teams.

evidence.quote: Math Center tutoring is available in person and online via Microsoft Teams.

question: can i get help studying for exams or understanding class material?
reference_answer: Yes. You can visit an Excel Center for exam prep, writing, math or science skills, and study strategies.

evidence.quote: Whether you need help preparing for an exam, improving your writing, strengthening math or science skills, or developing effective study strategies, you can visit an Excel Center whenever you need academic support.

question: how do i request disability accommodations at uccs?
reference_answer: Complete the application for accommodations and provide documentation.

evidence.quote: To initiate the process students should complete the application for accommodations and provide documentation.

question: do i need a doctors note to get accommodations?
reference_answer: Not to get started. Disability Services will meet with students who have no documentation or no formal diagnosis.

evidence.quote: Disability Services will meet with students who do not have documentation or who have not been formally diagnosed with a disability.

question: do i have to request my accommodations again every semester?
reference_answer: Yes. A Semester Request is needed to send your Faculty Accommodation Letters each semester.

evidence.quote: A Semester Request is needed to send Faculty Accommodation Letters to your faculty each semester

question: how do i let my professors know that i have approved accommodations?
reference_answer: Log in to the DS Portal and send an Accommodation Letter to each faculty member in your courses.

evidence.quote: Login to DS Portal to send Accommodation Letters to each faculty in your courses.

question: can i get extra time on exams if i have approved accommodations?
reference_answer: Yes, if extended time is approved. For online exams such as Canvas, you must tell your instructor before starting the exam.

evidence.quote: Students are responsible for communicating their approved extended time accommodations with their instructor prior to starting an online exam (i.e. Canvas).

question: how early do i need to schedule an exam with disability services?
reference_answer: At least 48 hours (2 business days) ahead. A Monday test must be scheduled by Thursday.

evidence.quote: Test appointments must be placed 48 hours (2 business days) in advance. Monday test appointments need to be scheduled by Thursday.

question: do i need to go to the testing center for an online exam?
reference_answer: Usually not. In most cases online exams are handled with the faculty member, with no need to schedule with the Testing Center.

evidence.quote: In most cases, online exams can be facilitated with the faculty; no need to schedule with the Testing Center.

question: can i request a different dorm room because of a disability?
reference_answer: You can request a housing accommodation, but a request does not guarantee a housing assignment.

evidence.quote: A request for housing accommodation does not guarantee a housing assignment.

question: what can i do if disability services denies my accommodation request?
reference_answer: If the request is denied through the informal appeal process, you can formally appeal by requesting a review of the determination.

evidence.quote: If a student requests a particular accommodation and the request has been denied through the informal appeal process, the student may formally appeal the decision by requesting a review of the determination.

question: where is disability services located and how can i contact them?
reference_answer: Main Hall, Room 324 (3rd floor). Phone (719) 255-3354, email dservice@uccs.edu.

evidence.quote: Location: Main Hall, Room 324 (3rd Floor) Phone: (719) 255-3354 Fax: (719) 255-3195 Email: dservice@uccs.edu

question: where can i go if i get sick or need to see a doctor on campus?
reference_answer: The Wellness Center, which offers in-person and telehealth appointments (telehealth for students living in Colorado).

evidence.quote: The Wellness Center offers in-person and telehealth appointments (for students that currently reside in Colorado).

question: how do i make an appointment at the uccs wellness center?
reference_answer: Call 719-255-4444 for all appointments.

evidence.quote: For all appointments, call 719-255-4444.

question: do i have to have health insurance to use the uccs wellness center?
reference_answer: No. UCCS does not require students to have health insurance, though it encourages credible coverage.

evidence.quote: UCCS does not require students to have health insurance. However, we do encourage all students to have credible insurance coverage

question: how much does it cost to see a doctor at the wellness center?
reference_answer: In-person and telehealth visits are $20.

evidence.quote: In-person and telehealth visits are $20.

question: can i talk to a doctor online instead of going to campus?
reference_answer: Yes, if you live in Colorado. Telehealth appointments are offered to students residing in Colorado.

evidence.quote: Medical/Health Services is currently offering in-person appointments, as well as telehealth appointments for students residing in Colorado.

question: what kind of medical services can i get at the uccs wellness center?
reference_answer: Care for acute illness, infections, injuries such as sprains, strains, joint pain, and head injuries, allergic reactions, and stomach problems, among others.

evidence.quote: Services offered: Acute illness, infections, injuries (sprains/strains, joint pain, head injury), allergic reactions, abdominal pain/nausea/vomiting/diarrhea, and more.

question: do i have to submit my vaccination records to uccs?
reference_answer: Yes. Colorado requires proof of immunity to measles, mumps, and rubella to attend classes at UCCS.

evidence.quote: The State of Colorado requires that you have proof of immunity to Measles, Mumps, and Rubella when attending classes at UCCS.

question: how many mmr shots do i need to show uccs?
reference_answer: Two. An official Certificate of Immunization signed by a physician, nurse, or school health authority must document two doses of MMR vaccine.

evidence.quote: Provide proof of immunity consisting of an official Certificate of Immunization, signed by a physician, nurse, or school health authority, which documents two doses of MMR vaccine.

question: do i need a meningitis vaccine if im living in the dorms?
reference_answer: If you are an incoming freshman living in housing, yes: provide proof of the Meningococcal ACWY vaccination or sign a waiver before move-in.

evidence.quote: all incoming Freshman living in housing must provide proof of receiving the Meningococcal ACWY vaccination or sign a waiver prior to move in.

question: where do i upload my vaccination records?
reference_answer: Through the Wellness Center Portal.

evidence.quote: Please submit immunizations to the Wellness Center via our Wellness Center Portal

question: can i get free counseling at uccs if im feeling stressed or overwhelmed?
reference_answer: Yes. The first three sessions are free, and additional sessions are $20 each.

evidence.quote: Students receive their first three sessions free of charge, and additional sessions are offered at an affordable rate of $20 per session.

question: how do i make an appointment with a uccs counselor?
reference_answer: Call the main line at (719) 255-4444 or visit the Wellness Center inside the Gallogly Recreation and Wellness Center.

evidence.quote: Students can begin services by calling our main line at (719) 255-4444 or by visiting the Wellness Center, located inside the Gallogly Recreation and Wellness Center.

question: does uccs offer group therapy or support groups?
reference_answer: Yes, and all of the groups cost $10 per visit.

evidence.quote: All of the groups cost $10 per visit.

question: is there someone i can talk to if im having a mental health crisis late at night?
reference_answer: Yes. UCCS students get free, confidential mental health support 24/7 through the Student Support app.

evidence.quote: UCCS students can get free, confidential mental health and wellbeing support 24/7 with the Student Support app.

question: can i meet with a nutritionist at uccs to get help with my diet?
reference_answer: Yes. UCCS students are eligible for 3 free nutrition counseling sessions with a registered dietitian.

evidence.quote: As a UCCS student, you are eligible for 3 free nutrition counseling sessions with our registered dietitian.

question: do i need a parking permit to park on campus?
reference_answer: Yes. All campus parking requires a permit or hourly payment unless specified otherwise.

evidence.quote: All campus parking requires a permit or hourly payment unless otherwise specified.

question: do i get a physical parking permit?
reference_answer: No. Permits are virtual: your license plate is your permit.

evidence.quote: Parking permits are now virtual permits, which is your license plate(s).

question: is there any free parking for students at uccs?
reference_answer: Yes, in the 500 series lots, but only after registering for the free 5S permit.

evidence.quote: Students and employees may park in the 500 series parking lots for free, but must register for the free 5S permit to do so.

question: what time do i have to start paying for parking at uccs?
reference_answer: Monday through Thursday, 8 am to 10 pm, and Friday, 8 am to 4 pm.

evidence.quote: Monday-Thursday: 8:00 am - 10:00 pm
Friday: 8:00 am - 4:00 pm

question: can i pay for parking with my phone instead of using the parking machines?
reference_answer: Yes. You can buy hourly or daily parking with the Parkmobile app.

evidence.quote: You may also purchase hourly/daily parking permits by using the third-party app "Parkmobile."

question: do i have to pay for parking on weekends?
reference_answer: No. Paid parking is not required on weekends, breaks between semesters, or holidays when classes are not in full session.

evidence.quote: Paid parking is not required on weekends, breaks between semesters, and on holidays when classes are not in full session.

question: when does the campus shuttle run?
reference_answer: Monday through Friday during the spring, fall, and summer semesters.

evidence.quote: Buses only run Monday - Friday during the Spring, Fall, and Summer semesters

question: how can i see where the uccs shuttle is?
reference_answer: The shuttles have GPS trackers that show their location on a map.

evidence.quote: The shuttles are fitted with GPS trackers that allow you to see their location on the map.

question: are the campus shuttles accessible for students who use wheelchairs?
reference_answer: Yes. All buses have mobility lifts.

evidence.quote: All buses have mobility lifts

question: who can get a mountain metro bus pass through uccs?
reference_answer: On-campus residents (picked up with their room key), a limited number of commuters on a first-come, first-served basis, and students with financial hardship or emergency transportation needs through the Dean of Students Office.

evidence.quote: On-campus residents (pick-up with room key). Limited commuter passes (first come-first-served) Students experiencing financial hardship or emergency transportation needs through the Dean of Students Office.

question: i live off campus, how can i request a mountain metro bus pass?
reference_answer: Request one through Parking. Commuter passes are limited and given out first come, first served.

evidence.quote: Off-Campus Residents Request a pass through parking.
Limited commuter passes (first come-first-served)

question: i got a parking ticket but i think it was a mistake, can i appeal it?
reference_answer: Yes. Appeal it through the Parking Portal within 10 days of the citation date.

evidence.quote: Visit the Parking Portal to pay or appeal a citation.
Parking citations must be paid or appealed within 10 days of the date of the citation or an additional $10 late fee will be assessed to the citation.

question: what happens if i dont pay my parking ticket on time?
reference_answer: If it is not paid or appealed within 10 days of the citation date, a $10 late fee is added.

evidence.quote: Parking citations must be paid or appealed within 10 days of the date of the citation or an additional $10 late fee will be assessed to the citation.
